top.title: Sparta UFC vet Jim Miller blends family, farming, fighting | Exclusive
top.description: Jim Miller hasn't changed much during his long mixed martial arts career. There might not be butterflies as Miller takes his 48th walk to face Terrance McKinney in UFC's Octagon on Nov. 14 in New York City. But the 43-year-old from Sparta remains just as steady and hardworking as in his pro debut almost exactly 21 years ago. The only one to fight at UFC 100, 200 and 300 , Miller (39-19, 1 NC) holds UFC records for most bouts, wins and submission attempts. He earned his first UFC submission in the third round of his first fight with the organization back in October 2008. "To think back to those beginning days, it's a lifetime ago," Miller said in an exclusive interview on Tuesday, shortly after arriving at a midtown Manhattan hotel for UFC 334 Fight Week. "I'm a competitor. I've been an athlete my whole life. I somehow found a way to continue on into my 40s. Very few people have that opportunity. I've been trying to make the most of it." Quick ending ahead? Miller is 11 years older, two inches shorter, and has a two-inch reach disadvantage against McKinney. But he's not worried about those numbers. His challenge on Saturday at Madison Square Garden is to match McKinney's aggressiveness and power right from the start. McKinney (18-9) has a first-round finish in all but one of his wins. But Miller has 17 first-round finishes of his own. Longtime trainer Brian McLaughlin said Miller's power has increased as he's aged. He believes Miller has the ability to knock McKinney out – quickly – with a hard shot. "Keep your eyes open. They're here for a good time, not a long time," McLaughlin said. "It's different with your pacing. You don't save your energy, because you're saving yourself for a round you're unlikely to see. ... You meet aggression with aggression, get ready for a sprint, and it becomes more instinctual and less strategic." Fighter and family man A wrestler since age 4, he remembers running on the roads in Lake Mohawk with his older brothers to get into shape. They also worked construction with their father, Mike Miller, who Jim called "a mountain of a man" at 6-foot-4 and 240 pounds who would "do physical, athletic things" on a job site and then come home and cook meals for the family. Jim Miller discovered MMA as an eighth grader after sneaking into a Bloomsburg University wrestling camp with his brothers. A coach played a VHS tape of an early UFC fight, and Jim thought, "Man, that's scary. I kind of want to do it." After wrestling at Sparta for four years, Miller dove into UFC online while at Virginia Tech. He and his brother Dan Miller decided to try it out, and both established careers. They also designed, built and opened their own training facility in Sparta in 2014. Now known as Sussex County MMA, that same space still serves as Jim Miller's year-round base. top.description: The De Pere boys basketball team has won five consecutive Fox River Classic Conference championships, and it will be one of the favorites again this season thanks in part to the return of Will Krueger. The league’s reigning player of the year made his collegiate future official Nov. 11 during National Signing Day. The 6-foot-5 senior shooting guard will play for Michigan Tech, an NCAA Division II school in Houghton. The Huskies went 29-7 last season and advanced to the Elite Eight of the NCAA DII Tournament. The 29 wins tied the program record. Some of the best players in program history have been local players, a list highlighted by former Ashwaubenon stars Kyle Monroe and Marcus Tomashek . Krueger should provide Michigan Tech with another solid scorer when he arrives in 2027-28. He has been a key figure for the Redbirds since his sophomore year and averaged a team-high 17.2 points along with 5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1 steal per game as a junior. Krueger shot 46.8% from 3-point range and has made 106 3-pointers in his career. “Will is a great teammate and his leadership will be extremely important to our success this year,” longtime De Pere basketball coach Brian Winchester said in a statement. “Will has worked hard to develop his talents and is very deserving of the opportunity at Michigan Tech. “Our coaching staff is extremely proud of Will and wish him continued success at MTU after a successful senior year and taking a run at another state title.” Krueger is one of several local athletes who will play at an NCAA Division I or II school and are expected to sign their letters of intent this week or next. top.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. "Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men's first-team head coach," the club said in a statement. "Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions." Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January. But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, the team have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings. Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago, with United yet to win a Premier League title since the retirement of the outstanding Scottish manager. top.description: Government workers in Osun resumed duty on Thursday after putting off their three-day warning strike called by the organiser labour for the release of funds due to local governments in the state by the Federal Government. The News of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates of the state government secretariat in Abere and Osun Assembly, shut since Monday, were reopened with workers back to work. Similarly, workers in Olorunda and Osogbo Local Government Secretariats were also back to their duty posts. NAN reports that organised labour in the state had on Sunday directed workers to embarked on solidarity strike with local government workers for the release of the withheld council allocations. The organised labour comprising the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC) and Joint Negotiating Council (JNC), however, on Wednesday directed workers to resume duty today. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. top.title: Rockstar workers vote on union recognition as GTA VI launch looms
top.description: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. nigeria.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
nigeria.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. nigeria.description: Indonesia’s vice president resigned Thursday, undone by a scandal over his high school diploma that has added to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. There had been repeated calls for Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, to step down following a Supreme Court ruling last month to annul his high school qualification, obtained abroad. Indonesia’s vice president does not have many constitutionally defined powers apart from acting as the president’s representative at official events and taking over if his boss is incapacitated. ‘Political realignment’ Gibran’s downfall came after thousands of Indonesians took to the streets in recent weeks to protest economic hardship, graft, perceived authoritarianism and the government’s handling of months of devastating wildfires emitting toxic haze. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing. – Iran, trade, China – That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. nigeria.title: Two Dead, Several Injured As New York Building Collapses
nigeria.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. Images from the scene showed firefighters sifting through a pile of rubble in front of what appeared to be a residential property with its walls torn down, exposing a bedroom and a clothing wardrobe. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people whom firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws. “We do not know how many people are still in the collapse zone, and this will be a prolonged operation,” FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters at the scene in Flatbush, Brooklyn late Wednesday. First responders tend to a collapsed building in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. She said two people had died, without disclosing their ages, and said 17 others were hurt, including seven children. Four people were critically injured. More than 250 firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, the FDNY wrote on X, adding that the cause of the collapse was under investigation. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised the emergency services for their work, saying the site involved “precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface.” “I want to ask New Yorkers to please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss,” he added at a news conference. New York Fire Department Chief John Esposito speaks next to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a press conference after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. One witness, named only as Anthony, told PIX11 News that he heard people screaming and a “bomb”-like noise as the building collapsed. Another witness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times: “The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell.” The city’s Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene “assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings.” Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of the department, said construction workers were performing excavation at the time of the collapse. He added that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building. nigeria.title: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
nigeria.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. With Huang unexpectedly on the backfoot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang. Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor. Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. nigeria.title: Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries
nigeria.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, and the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, have offered tips on how to stop the practice of students benefitting from the Student Loan Scheme and still going ahead to collect tuition fees from their parents and guardians. The practice, labelled double dipping by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which gives out the loans, is gradually becoming rampant and erasing the main reason the loan scheme was initiated – take the burden of tuition payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Speaking with Thursday Learning, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Deolu Ogunbanjo, opined that such a practice negates the reason for the setting up of the scheme. “The Student Loan Scheme was set up to give access to higher education to students who would otherwise drop out because of inability to pay fees. It is also to take the burden of fee payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Such happenings may not be totally eradicated. We know how rascally some young ones can be. “I think the way out is to let the parents and guardians be aware when payments are made by NELFUND to beneficiaries. Let there be a means of notifying the parents that their children have benefitted from the scheme,” he said Similarly, the National Public Relations Officer of NANS, Comrade Obidah David, also supported notification being sent to parents of beneficiaries. “If it is a text message, they can send to parents and guardians of beneficiaries. Information on contacts of parents is always provided by students when registering. That is necessary in case of any emergency. Also, names of beneficiaries can be published whether in the traditional media or social media. There is nothing bad in that. It is for transparency, “ he stated. Recall that recently, the Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said during a press briefing that the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from NELFUND and still stressing their parents. We are going to put an end to that,” he said. Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, maintaining the wider spread observed earlier in the week. At the official window, data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the naira entering Thursday’s session around the ₦1,350.36 to ₦1,353.50 per dollar band. Early Thursday morning international currency feeds recorded spot quotes hovering near ₦1,345.72 per dollar, while official NFEM benchmarks reflect the closing figures from the prior trading session pending the day’s official fixing. Earlier in the week, trading at the official window saw intraday fluctuations between ₦1,349.25 and ₦1,354 per dollar, with interbank turnover reaching $248.07 million across 144 deals. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a significant discount to the official rate. Currency dealers across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,411 and ₦1,420 for buying, while selling rates ranged from ₦1,419 to ₦1,430 per dollar depending on transaction volume and location. This leaves an exchange rate gap of roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and street-level rates. Market analysts attribute the recent softening of the local currency to heightened seasonal foreign exchange demand from importers and travelers heading into the end-of-year period, alongside foreign portfolio investment outflows and a firmer US dollar globally. Despite the recent dip—which saw the parallel market touch a 10-month low of ₦1,430 per dollar this week—Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain sturdy at approximately $54.9 billion, well above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion, offering a substantial buffer to support market liquidity through the remainder of the fourth quarter. Traders and businesses continue to monitor daily NFEM liquidity injections and CBN updates for direction as Thursday’s trading progresses. nigeria.description: By Morenike Taire Joy Odimegwu, a University of Lagos academic in the Department of Pharmacognosy, Faculty of Pharmacy, is a senior researcher with over 20 years of international experience with a passion for translating herbal medicine drug discovery from labs to markets to solve some of the world’s most pressing health care challenges, including drug resistant gynecological cancers and pain. As a fellow of Mujeres Por Africa and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, she sits at the intersection between biodiversity and cutting edge technology. With a PhD in herbal medicine, Odimegwu is a herbal medicine expert who got a grant from Gates Foundation to train African researchers on women’s health. For many years they have been using broccoli to prevent certain gynecological cancers so as a researcher, I wanted to know what was in it. nigeria.title: How ISWAP’s southern expansion plot was foiled, commander killed in Ondo forest
nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, also known as Anwar, a senior commander of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), alongside several of his fighters has brought major relief not only to the people of Ondo State but to the entire southern Nigeria. Ohida, who took over the coordination of ISWAP’s central and southern regional activities following the 2023 arrest of his superior, Abu Ikrimah (Abu Uwais) inside an Ondo forest, was killed during an intelligence-led operation deep inside the Owo Forest, Ondo State, early this month. Despite this breakthrough however, former Secretary to the Government of the Federation and now traditional ruler of Ilu-Abo in Akure North, Oba Olu Falae, has lamented that kidnapping and banditry still hold sway in rural communities The operation was executed by a combined team of Nigerian Army troops, operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), and officers of the Western Nigeria Security Network, codenamed Amotekun, with strategic intelligence backing from the United Kingdom. A major blow against southern expansion, security analysts have described the operation as another major counter-terrorism breakthrough by Nigerian security agencies, at a time authorities are intensifying efforts to prevent terrorist groups from extending their operational footprint from the North-East into the South. According to security sources, the forces carried out a thorough clearance operation in the forest, aimed at dislodging entrenched terrorist cells and preventing planned attacks on communities in southern Nigeria. Before the breakthrough, credible intelligence had indicated that Ohida was plotting to launch coordinated attacks on civilians during the festive period. The plot was designed to create a widespread atmosphere of insecurity that could undermine public confidence and disrupt preparations for the 2027 general elections. His elimination has therefore foiled the group’s plans to launch major terrorist attacks in parts of southern Nigeria during the coming festivities. The killing of Ohida came barely months after Nigerian and United States forces, in a joint counter-terrorism operation, killed another senior Islamic State commander, Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, in Borno State. For years, Ohida’s group had carried out several coordinated attacks against military formations, security installations and other soft targets as part of a deliberate strategy to establish or expand operational networks outside its traditional strongholds in northeastern Nigeria. The latest operation is being viewed by security authorities as a decisive attempt to disrupt ISWAP’s desperate push to establish a new operational corridor in the South. nigeria.title: 4 dead, many hospitalised in Benue after consuming herbal mixture
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru Makurdi —No fewer than four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are battling for their lives in hospital after allegedly consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. It was gathered that the incident occurred after three men, identified as Magani, Mohamed and Kala, allegedly sold herbal preparations suspected to contain poisonous substances to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju township, last weekend. According to the eyewitness, “The development gained attention when some of those, who drank the mixture and their loved ones raised the alarm on November 2, 2026, after several residents, who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations started developing similar symptoms. “While the first victim reportedly died Tuesday morning, the second died in the early hours of Wednesday, and the third and fourth victims died later on November 4, 2026. “As we speak, over 14 other victims are currently battling for their lives, with many of them said to be in critical condition.” He disclosed that the three suspects allegedly involved in the sale of the herbal mixture were apprehended by the leadership of the Igede Youth Council, in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership, and subsequently handed over to the police in Oju. “We have been told that the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters has transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command, where the suspects are currently undergoing investigation,” he said. Speaking while handing over the suspects to the police, President of the Igede Youth Council, John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State government to ensure a thorough investigation of the incident and guarantee that justice was served. Ozzidi said the Igede youths had deliberately refrained from taking the law into their hands, resisting the temptation to subject the suspects to jungle justice. He explained that their decision to allow the law to take its course demonstrated their confidence in the state government to ensure justice is done in the matter. The youth leader also urged political officeholders from the area to follow up on the case to ensure that the deceased victims got justice and that the circumstances surrounding the suspected poisoning were fully established. Contacted, the Chairman of Oju council, Mr. Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he was yet to obtain the exact number of fatalities. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, Peter Aondongu, for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to enquiries at press time. business.title: MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30 MSCI will remove Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, from the MSCI USA Index as of the close of Nov. 30, the index provider said Wednesday, after a new screen classified the company as a non-operating issuer. The decision is part of MSCI’s November 2026 Index Review , posted shortly after 5 p.m. ET. Official additions and deletions lists show Strategy (MSTR) out of its USA Index, which also takes it out of the broader MSCI World and ACWI indexes. The same review deletes Japan’s Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the MSCI United Kingdom Small Cap Index, and it removes Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag from the MSCI Iceland Frontier Markets Small Cap Index and micro-cap Upexi from the USA Micro Cap Index. All five had already been marked Deleted on MSCI’s potential-impact list , built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values. Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and, on that October list, accounted for more than 90% of the five companies’ combined float-adjusted market value. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin, or $64.16 billion in aggregate. Strategy shares closed at $122.35, up 1.06%, then slipped 1.51% to $120.50 in after-hours trading as of 5:34 p.m. ET. How the MSCI screen works The rule does not mention bitcoin. The index first checks whether a company’s operating assets equal at least 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail that core screen face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the ineligibility screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. The index said it may also use the most recent interim filing. MSCI also said Wednesday that the same non-operating treatment will apply to the MSCI US Index Series. The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. The index first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. It adopted the new methodology on Oct. 15, with minor modifications, and said it would end the interim measures it had placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions. What the deletion does and does not do Funds that track an MSCI index have to hold what the index holds, so they will have to sell the deleted stocks by the Nov. 30 close. entertainment.title: Olumide Oworu Declares House of Representatives Bid for Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027
entertainment.description: Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot. Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”. Olumide Oworu is contesting for a legislative seat in Surulere Constituency 1 under the APM platform. entertainment.description: Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors coordinating in neutral tones and a red cap accent for AFRIFF. Who knew an ivory mini dress and a classic black suit could make such an interesting pairing? During their time in Lagos for AFRIFF, Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors posed for a studio portrait in two looks that took very different approaches to dressing up. Meagan’s dress brought together colourful beadwork, a fitted silhouette and a floor-length train, while Jonathan opted for black tailoring, an open-neck white shirt and a red cap. And while his outfit keeps things relatively simple, there’s nothing ordinary about the details of hers. Let’s start with Meagan’s dress, because there is quite a lot happening here. At first glance, the ivory mini might seem relatively simple, but look a little closer and the details begin to unfold. The fitted halter-neck bodice is covered in rows of turquoise, bronze and dark green beads, arranged horizontally to follow the shape of her waist. Then there’s the skirt, which takes a more unexpected turn with clusters of dark beaded embellishments scattered across the fabric. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. Read what AI produces, question its suggestions and make the final decisions yourself. Your skills improve when you practise them, not when you consistently hand them over to a machine. Arriving in San Juan on Monday, 9 November, Danielle joins nearly 120 delegates from across the globe for preliminary rounds, national costume presentations, and rehearsals. sports.title: Sparta UFC vet Jim Miller blends family, farming, fighting | Exclusive
sports.description: Jim Miller hasn't changed much during his long mixed martial arts career. There might not be butterflies as Miller takes his 48th walk to face Terrance McKinney in UFC's Octagon on Nov. 14 in New York City. But the 43-year-old from Sparta remains just as steady and hardworking as in his pro debut almost exactly 21 years ago. The only one to fight at UFC 100, 200 and 300 , Miller (39-19, 1 NC) holds UFC records for most bouts, wins and submission attempts. He earned his first UFC submission in the third round of his first fight with the organization back in October 2008. "To think back to those beginning days, it's a lifetime ago," Miller said in an exclusive interview on Tuesday, shortly after arriving at a midtown Manhattan hotel for UFC 334 Fight Week. "I'm a competitor. I've been an athlete my whole life. I somehow found a way to continue on into my 40s. Very few people have that opportunity. I've been trying to make the most of it." Quick ending ahead? Miller is 11 years older, two inches shorter, and has a two-inch reach disadvantage against McKinney. But he's not worried about those numbers. His challenge on Saturday at Madison Square Garden is to match McKinney's aggressiveness and power right from the start. McKinney (18-9) has a first-round finish in all but one of his wins. But Miller has 17 first-round finishes of his own. Longtime trainer Brian McLaughlin said Miller's power has increased as he's aged. He believes Miller has the ability to knock McKinney out – quickly – with a hard shot. "Keep your eyes open. They're here for a good time, not a long time," McLaughlin said. "It's different with your pacing. You don't save your energy, because you're saving yourself for a round you're unlikely to see. ... You meet aggression with aggression, get ready for a sprint, and it becomes more instinctual and less strategic." Fighter and family man A wrestler since age 4, he remembers running on the roads in Lake Mohawk with his older brothers to get into shape. They also worked construction with their father, Mike Miller, who Jim called "a mountain of a man" at 6-foot-4 and 240 pounds who would "do physical, athletic things" on a job site and then come home and cook meals for the family. Jim Miller discovered MMA as an eighth grader after sneaking into a Bloomsburg University wrestling camp with his brothers. A coach played a VHS tape of an early UFC fight, and Jim thought, "Man, that's scary. I kind of want to do it." After wrestling at Sparta for four years, Miller dove into UFC online while at Virginia Tech. He and his brother Dan Miller decided to try it out, and both established careers. They also designed, built and opened their own training facility in Sparta in 2014. Now known as Sussex County MMA, that same space still serves as Jim Miller's year-round base. sports.title: Local high school athletes make college plans official on National Signing Day
sports.description: The De Pere boys basketball team has won five consecutive Fox River Classic Conference championships, and it will be one of the favorites again this season thanks in part to the return of Will Krueger. The league’s reigning player of the year made his collegiate future official Nov. 11 during National Signing Day. The 6-foot-5 senior shooting guard will play for Michigan Tech, an NCAA Division II school in Houghton. The Huskies went 29-7 last season and advanced to the Elite Eight of the NCAA DII Tournament. The 29 wins tied the program record. Some of the best players in program history have been local players, a list highlighted by former Ashwaubenon stars Kyle Monroe and Marcus Tomashek . Krueger should provide Michigan Tech with another solid scorer when he arrives in 2027-28. He has been a key figure for the Redbirds since his sophomore year and averaged a team-high 17.2 points along with 5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1 steal per game as a junior. Krueger shot 46.8% from 3-point range and has made 106 3-pointers in his career. “Will is a great teammate and his leadership will be extremely important to our success this year,” longtime De Pere basketball coach Brian Winchester said in a statement. “Will has worked hard to develop his talents and is very deserving of the opportunity at Michigan Tech. “Our coaching staff is extremely proud of Will and wish him continued success at MTU after a successful senior year and taking a run at another state title.” Krueger is one of several local athletes who will play at an NCAA Division I or II school and are expected to sign their letters of intent this week or next. Ashwaubenon Emma Kozloski will compete in swimming at DII Quincy University in Illinois. The senior will be busy at the WIAA Division 2 state meet this week. She is set to compete in the 100-yard breaststroke and the 200-yard individual medley and was part of 200 freestyle and 400 freestyle relay teams that won sectional championships. Bay Port Karlie Schock will play tennis at the University of Michigan. She made history as a freshman in 2023 when she became the first local D1 girls player to win a state title since the tournament started in 1971 while becoming the first since Racine Case’s Bojana Pozder in 2018 to not drop a single set at state. Schock returned for her sophomore season with hopes of leading Bay Port to state, but when that goal fell short after the Pirates’ runner-up sectional finish, she opted to not defend her state title at the individual tournament and instead compete in a USTA junior event. She did not play high school tennis her final two seasons but is one of the best players in the state. Her commitment to the Wolverines keeps the family tradition alive. sports.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
sports.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. "Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men's first-team head coach," the club said in a statement. "Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions." Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January. But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, the team have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings. Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago, with United yet to win a Premier League title since the retirement of the outstanding Scottish manager. technology.title: Orbit Global Menu: A working global menu addon for GNOME
technology.description: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all. Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it. There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps. The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works. It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications. The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither. The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. technology.title: London hotel put admin login for booking website on whiteboard behind the front desk
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where all the victims are self-owned. This week, we welcome you to a London hotel where you could check out its admin credentials for a booking website just by walking past the front desk. Our story comes courtesy of Neycho Tepavicharov, co-founder of Flashcloud, a Delaware-based web hosting company. He was staying at a hotel in London when he noticed a shocking breach of basic security protocols by management, who were a little too hospitable with their credentials. As he was passing through the lobby, Tepavicharov noticed that the door behind the front desk was open and, inside that back room, there was a whiteboard. On the whiteboard, written in plain English, were the hotel’s Booking.com administrative username and password. Anyone near the desk could clearly see the login information, and if they didn’t have time to write it down, they could have snapped a picture for later use. As Tepavicharov explains, there’s plenty of mischief you could perform with these credentials. “With that login, someone could change or cancel reservations, see guests’ names and contact details, or message guests pretending to be the hotel,” he said. “Fake 'please confirm your payment' messages sent from compromised hotel accounts are a well-known scam.” An attacker could potentially exploit that access to disrupt hotel operations or target guests with convincing scams. Whether the exposed credentials alone would have been enough to access the account would depend on its security settings. Tepavicharov decided to play the role of good samaritan and warn the hotel’s manager that the business was endangering itself by showing everyone its password. “I asked to speak with the manager and showed him what I’d seen. He was mortified and very grateful,” Tepavicharov said. “Nobody on staff had thought of it as a risk. It was just the easiest way for the whole team to share one login.” After Tepavicharov talked to the manager, not only did the hotel change its ways, but it also moved its website to his hosting service, Flashcloud. Tepavicharov notes that there are plenty of takeaways from this incident. Most important: give each user dedicated credentials with their own separate login, and use multi-factor authentication. “The lesson is an old one, but it keeps happening,” he said. “Shared logins end up written somewhere convenient. Give each staff member their own login, turn on two-factor authentication, and keep passwords in a password manager, not on the wall.” ®

technology.title: Data sovereignty takes more than keeping data close to home
technology.description: Keeping sensitive data within national borders might satisfy a residency requirement. But does it mean your organization is genuinely in control? Not necessarily. Data could be stored locally while remaining subject to another jurisdiction's laws, dependent on overseas service providers or exposed to disruption beyond your control. For enterprise IT teams, that distinction is becoming harder to ignore. Geopolitical tensions, evolving regulations and the growing use of AI are forcing organizations to reconsider what data sovereignty means in practice. Yet translating those concerns into a workable strategy is another matter. And simply throwing more money at the problem won't necessarily solve it. In The Register's on-demand webinar, Data Sovereignty By Design, moderator Tim Phillips speaks with Patrick Smith, Field CTO for EMEA at Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, about moving beyond compliance checklists and taking a more strategic approach to data control. Drawing on findings from Everpure's research, Smith explores a curious disconnect: organizations are increasing their investment in sovereignty initiatives, yet many still lack a coordinated strategy. Some of the risks attracting the most attention aren't necessarily those receiving the greatest investment. The discussion examines why sovereignty shouldn't be treated as an IT-only responsibility. Decisions about which data needs protection, which services must remain operational and what level of risk is acceptable require input from business leaders, security, procurement and legal teams. There's also the question of priorities. Not every workload needs the same sovereign controls, and attempting to protect everything equally can make an already complicated challenge considerably harder. Smith explains the concept of the "minimum viable company," identifying the critical services, applications and data an organization needs to keep operating through disruption. He also considers why visibility into data access, supplier dependencies and potential exit strategies should influence technology decisions from the outset. For IT leaders trying to turn sovereignty from an abstract boardroom concern into something actionable, the conversation offers useful questions to take back to their organizations. Because knowing where your data sits is one thing. Knowing whether you can maintain control when circumstances change is quite another. technology.title: Your AI agent is only as good as your endpoint data
technology.description: Every so often a flaw comes along that shows how fast the ground can shift under IT and security teams. PHP2Shell, a pair of critical flaws in PHP, was one of them. Details leaked before the planned disclosure, frontier AI helped researchers find the flaws, and PHP shipped fixes the next day. For many teams, though, the patch was the easy part. So what does it take to respond at that speed, and where should teams begin? What does governed autonomous IT look like in practice? Picture a loop. Software finds where a risk lives and ranks what matters most. It proposes a fix, then, inside limits people define, carries it out and checks that it worked. Routine, low-risk actions can run on their own. Higher-impact ones wait for a person to approve. A few are never handed over at all. Each step leaves a record that someone can review and reverse. What challenges do IT and security teams face today? Three problems keep coming up. The first is visibility. PHP2Shell reportedly sat undetected for more than a decade. For these two flaws, the fix was a version upgrade. The hard part was finding every copy of PHP, including copies bundled inside other software or extracted by hand onto Windows machines that never registered as installed applications. Then teams had to work out which copies the internet could reach and check for signs of earlier attack. An inventory built from a periodic snapshot can't answer those questions on the day they matter. The second is tool-hopping. Answering "where does this run, and can the internet reach it?" often means pivoting across an asset inventory, a vulnerability scanner and an external attack surface tool, each with its own view. Every hop adds delay. Every console is another chance to disagree with the last. The third is pace. Several security firms reported exploitation attempts before PHP released its fixes, and Cloudflare reported early attacks hours ahead of the patch. technology.title: AWS distills its cloud into a local emulator that runs on your PC
technology.description: AWS has released an emulator that kind-of-almost lets you use its cloud on a PC. As explained in the GitHub repository for the prosaically named “AWS Emulator,” the tool “is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint.” The emulator doesn’t replicate the whole AWS cloud, instead offering its APIs. “You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI),” the repo explains. Because those tests never touch the AWS cloud, the tool is free to use. AWS wrote the emulator in Rust, a choice that senior specialist solutions architect Daniel Abib wrote helps to ensure the tool “stays light on CPU and memory on a laptop.” The emulator tool doesn’t replicate the entire AWS cloud. Abib said it supports the APIs of AWS services that have an API model in the AWS API models repository on GitHub . The Register found over 1,300 items on that page. While the tool lets developers test APIs, it doesn’t replicate anywhere near all the features of the Amazonian cloud. “It doesn’t evaluate IAM [Identity and Access Management] policies the way AWS does, and each emulator acts as a single account, with no cross-account or cross-Region behavior,” Abib wrote, adding “How closely it matches AWS varies by service and feature.” AWS publishes “fidelity scores” that detail how closely the emulator works on different AWS services. Amazon tries to achieve full fidelity, so the emulator produces the same results as AWS for valid API calls, and the same errors for invalid ones. Coding agents can also drive the Emulator, an option The Register mentions because AWS advises the easiest way to check if a project will work with the tool is to use the aws-emulator skill for AI coding agents. “With the skill, your agent finds the AWS operations and resources that your project depends on. It checks them against the fidelity tests and fidelity scores for the emulator. It then tells you which parts of your project you can rely on the emulator for, and which ones might behave differently from AWS,” according to AWS documentation. AWS has made the emulator available as an RPM or Debian package. Mac and PC users will need to run Docker and an image of the Emulator. “You install the emulator, start it, and point your tools at the local endpoint,” Abib instructed. “When AWS Emulator starts, it generates its own credentials, a config file, and a certificate, and writes them to ~/.aws/emulator/9297/ . You set environment variables so the AWS SDK talks to your laptop instead of AWS, and your application code stays unchanged.” “From there, your existing tests, CLI scripts, and coding agents keep working the way they already do. technology.title: Disgraced former CA eMudhra blames buggy script for hopelessly weak certificates
technology.description: Former certification authority eMudhra has claimed a buggy Python script is the main reason it issued laughably insecure digital certificates. The company posted its account of the matter on Bugzilla where a user with the handle “Naveen Kumar ML” wrote “During a single key‑generation ceremony on 30 April 2025, sixteen subordinate (issuing) CA key pairs in eMudhra’s ‘B’ and ‘C’ series were generated correctly on a hardware security module and then processed through an approved wrap/unwrap round‑trip using a custom python key‑handling script.” eMudhra aimed to create eight ECDSA P-384 private keys which should have been 48 bytes long. But the script contained what Kumar described as “a bug/defect in the import code [which] resulted in a read‑back from the unwrapped object that truncated the private value, so the certified public keys correspond to private scalars below the expected range and are recoverable from public information.” The truncation is the key problem here, because it appears that eMudhra ignored 47 of the 48 bytes, producing its infamously insecure single-byte keys such as the number four. Whatever the nature of the bug, Kumar asserts it was “a custom script run only on an isolated ceremony host and was not a function of the emCA software.” eMudhra needed that script because “global supply chain constraints” meant it couldn’t acquire the hardware security modules (HSMs), devices that generate and store cryptographic keys, that it wanted to use when creating a set of certificates for use in the USA. It therefore used HSMs made by a company called Utimaco to generate keys and planned to transfer the keys it produced to a different set of HSMs from a company called Crypto4A. Kumar explained that eMudhra decided on that move, which is unusual, because changes to policy about provenance of certificates meant it had to generate new certs by the end of May. The plan went sour when the company didn’t notice the errors in its script and didn’t test the keys it created. The rest is history: a Mozilla team member noticed that the company’s keys were woefully weak and pointed out that attackers could therefore issue fraudulent certificates that allowed them to impersonate servers, observe traffic, or even modify data in transit. Browser-makers quickly tweaked their software so it would not recognize certs from eMudhra. The Indian business then quit the SSL/TLS certification business, which it said was never a major source of revenue but had suddenly become a severe source of embarrassment. Kumar’s new post lists three steps eMudhra will take to wind up its certification business, one of which will see the company “Put in place improvements motivated by findings of [an] independent review to strengthen our general PKI operations.” Sounds like a plan. ®

technology.title: Russian cloud Yandex says drone attacks on its datacenters caused data loss
technology.description: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex’s ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company’s cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on “critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform.” It’s unclear if Yandex’s use of the phrase “on the platform” indicates it doesn’t keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don’t create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn’t protect their data. Whatever happened, Yandex has decided to enable backups by default for all VMs customers create in its cloud. That decision will mean customers will consume and pay for more Yandex resources, unless they opt out of the automated backups. Given that drones damaged three Yandex locations, and the war with Ukraine continues, users have good reasons to consider alternatives to its services. Indeed, Yandex’s announcement of its recovery efforts links to a page extolling the virtues of a hybrid cloud when devising data protection strategies. That page also mentions Yandex’s own Stackland product, which brings its stack on-prem, as an example of a hybrid approach. On Wednesday the company also launched a new availability zone named ru-central1-f. Yandex didn’t say where it’s located, other than to say it’s in “a new location.” Interestingly, Yandex has imposed quotas that limit the amount of resources users can access in the new availability zone and says it can’t yet handle traffic to private endpoints at the new facility. Many nations have imposed sanctions that restrict sales of technology products to Russia. It’s therefore unsurprising that Yandex might struggle to provision enough infrastructure to allow untrammeled access to a new availability zone. ®

science.title: Scotland’s Flow Country
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Scotland’s Flow Country Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search March 4, 2024 Compared to ecosystems in many other parts of the world, the blanket bogs of the Flow Country in northern Scotland are unassuming—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses, and heathers. Yet, to ecologists, the seemingly desolate areas are nothing short of extraordinary. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon . That’s because their soils are so waterlogged that microbes cannot fully break down dead plant material, a process that would otherwise release carbon dioxide. Instead, partially decayed plant matter accumulates into thick layers of spongy, crumbly, carbon-rich material called peat . The unusual ecosystems, also called blanket mires and featherbed bogs, only occur in places with abundant rainfall, poor drainage, and low levels of evapotranspiration . These types of bogs cover just 120,000 square kilometers (46,000 square miles) globally, less than one-tenth of one percent of Earth’s land surface. The image above, captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 , is centered on blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands, home to the largest such ecosystem in Europe. This peatland is also the first of its type to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site . The peat bogs of northern Scotland, home to more than 30 species of sphagnum moss , are spread across some 1,900 square kilometers (730 square miles) of the country’s Highlands region. In this image, boggy areas appear dark brown and are sprinkled with lakes. The light green area on the right side around Thurso is farmland. The darker green geometric patterns in the center are conifer plantations . The image was captured in the spring, the part of the year when the land surface is most waterlogged and peat bogs begin to accumulate large amounts of new biomass. While forests store most of their carbon in living trees—which eventually release it back into the atmosphere when they burn or die—peat bogs often store carbon for many thousands of years. Some parts of the Flow Country have been accumulating peat for more than 9,000 years, building deposits exceeding eight meters thick, according to UNESCO. Overall, scientists estimate that all of the world’s peatlands cover just 3 percent of Earth’s land surface but store more than 600 gigatons of carbon—about twice as much as all the world’s forests combined. science.title: Some PFAS chemicals are declining in English rivers but others are appearing
science.description: The River Wye in Derbyshire, England Dave Porter/Alamy The concentration of two of the most well-studied PFAS forever chemicals are showing a strong downward trend in English rivers. The finding adds to a mixed story for the power of global restrictions. The levels of perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in English rivers have fallen by 30 per cent and 29 per cent, respectively, over the past decade, according to a new report by scientists at the Environment Agency (EA) , a UK government green regulator. Both of these human-made chemicals take a long time to break down in the environment. The International Agency for Research on Cancer recently designated PFOA as carcinogenic to humans , and both forever chemicals have been linked to reproductive health and developmental impacts as well as other serious health issues. Advertisement Read more Fish-based pet food may expose cats and dogs to forever chemicals Under the United Nations Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, the use of PFOS was restricted from 2009, and the use of PFOA was restricted from 2019 – although there were country-specific caveats on which uses they applied to. They had both been used in non-stick coatings on consumer products as well as in industrial processes. Both were also used in firefighting foams, a major source of PFAS pollution entering the environment, with a ban on PFOA in firefighting foams only coming into force in the UK in 2025. Rob Bradburne , the EA’s chief scientist, describes his group’s results as proof that the global ban was “a really positive move”. But, he adds that the huge range of PFAS chemicals is going to “complicate the story”. An issue that is clear in the dataset for England is that while these two main PFAS have declined, many other “forever chemicals” that are being used to replace them – such as short-chain PFAS and fluorotelomer compounds – have now emerged in the environment at detectable levels. science.description: null A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled Mars Sample Return (MSR) program, called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture, or PSRA in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. The PSRA initiative was noted on Nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG). Here's the PSRA strategy: Develop impartial recommendations for retrieving the Martian samples collected by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover and deliver them to Earth Assess proposed mission requirements Review prior lessons learned Evaluate current capabilities and acquisition options Morgan noted that there will be a PSRA strategy team kickoff in January 2027 with a final report due in winter 2027-2028. Pick-me-ups The backdrop to the PSRA activity is that there's one busy rover already on the Red Planet snagging and bagging samples. NASA's Perseverance Mars rover remains on the prowl within Jezero Crater following its touchdown in February 2021. That car-sized robot has been grabbing select specimens from across the area and gingerly dropping the sealed pick-me-ups on the surface of Mars , as well as stuffing them inside the rover itself. Those collectibles may well hold signs of past life on the enigmatic, dusty and foreboding Red Planet. NASA and the European Space Agency have for years been intently plotting out plans to send future spacecraft to Mars and haul those Perseverance-plucked bits, pieces, and sniffs of atmosphere to Earth for rigorous inspection here on Earth using state-of-the-art equipment. This photomontage shows each of the sample tubes deposited by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover at the Three Forks sample depot, as viewed by the WATSON camera on the end of the rover's robotic arm. That finding was deemed by NASA itself as too costly and not doable within an acceptable time frame. science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website , the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. An animation shows the random appearance of fast radio bursts (FRBs) across the sky (Image credit: NRAO Outreach/T. Jarrett (IPAC/Caltech); B. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space.com by email.
